newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay market breaks barrier, hits 33-month high.
newsitem.headline: Bombay market breaks barrier, hits 33-month high.

text.p: Bombay shares broke through a psychological barrier to reach new 33-month highs on Wednesday propelled by heavy foreign fund buying, brokers said.
"There's been frenzied buying by FIIs (foreign institutional investors)," said Sanat Dalal, a broker at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). "They are accumulating all the blue chips."
The benchmark 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) index leapt 96.41 points, or 2.24 percent, to a provisional close of 4,402.80 -- piercing the 4,400 level for the first time since mid-October 1994.
"It has crossed the barrier. The market looks in very good shape," said Ketan Jhaveri, chief dealer at Kotak Securities, the Indian affiliate of Goldman Sachs.
Analysts said expectations of improved corporate results during fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) were attracting investors.

"Corporate India seems to be signalling a better year in FY1998 (financial year ending March 31, 1998) based on our analysis of the results of nearly 250 companies," Pravin Shah at Morgan Stanley Dean Witter said in a report.
Traders said the buoyant market lured more investors while sellers were becoming more choosy.
"The biggest point to note is that the most prominent seller has stopped selling," said Dalal, referring to the Unit Trust of India, the country's largest mutual fund.
Other dealers said foreign funds were enlarging their portfolio by buying into new sectors.
The National Stock Exchange (NSE) index gained 36.10 points, or 3.0 percent, to a provisional 1,238.90.
"The FIIs are strengthening their portfolio by adding multinational shares to other blue chips," said Arun Shah, chief dealer at brokerage P.R. Subramanyan & Sons. RG/SK
